title: The reference run plays the game the tutorial teaches: rations get made, the belt carries the coal, and the city grows across three days instead of dying with 5 of 5 machines stalled

the_question_i_was_asked.was the frozen kitchen and sorter my sce: MINE, and the diagnosis is exact. The field kitchen and rubble sorter produced nothing because BOTH COAL GENERATORS WERE FROZEN AT THE FINAL TICK WITH FULL BUNKERS (63.0 and 57.6 of a 63 capacity). They stood at (124,142) and (129,145), 14 and 17 tiles from the Hearth's footprint, where its warmth field is worth about 3 C. A coal generator holds itself at (ground + 11 C) and freezes below -10, so it needs ground warmer than about -21 C; this map's ambient bottoms out at -32.85. Once frozen its radiance_factor() returns 0, so it stops radiating, so it can only thaw on somebody ELSE's warmth — which is why neither ever came back. Supply was therefore the Hearth alone: 138.88 against 190.89 of demand. [P02] sheds by priority tier and industry is 50 while housing is 90, so a 27% shortfall did not brown the city out evenly, it took EVERY unit away from the factory: rubble_sorter read `power 0.0000` at all eight checkpoints of the run. No grain, so `field_kitchen` read `missing_input: grain` for eleven thousand ticks, so half rations at t15230, so hope 0.00 at t20420, so the player exiled at t22380. One under-built grid and the whole run falls out of it in that order. economy_60min had this law written down under THE WARMTH-COVER LAW and first_night had never applied it.

what_the_layout_now_is: SUPPLY FIRST AND WARM. Six burners standing two to three tiles off the Hearth's north and south faces, where its field is still worth 20 to 28 C. Every position in this scenario was checked against the smoothstep falloff in game/sim/heat/warmth_field.gd at the coldest ambient the run reaches, because warmth — not proximity to a pipe — is the placement rule: a 1-unit watchtower needs +20 C of radiated cover to survive a -32 C night and a 9-unit housing block needs none.

ONE BELT, FIVE BUNKERS AND THE HEARTH. A coal yard at (113,120), a line down the burner row, and four arms off the Hearth's south face fed by a crate the porters keep topped up through a standing `request`. [P03] stands the porters down for any burner an arm is feeding, so this is a real bet and not a decoration.

A SUNKEN BELT PAIR at x126/x129 so two heat mains can cross the line at x127 and x128. A belt is a wall: it owns every tile of its row and without the tunnel there is no square left for heat to get from the salvage strip down to the burner main.
THE SALVAGE STRIP, radiator-first: two sorters (one on salvaged_stores for grain, one on sorted_rubble for the smelter's ore), a collector and the kitchen, all inside a radiator's face.

A DRILL ON THE COAL SEAM AT (124,97). Measured, not guessed: a throwaway probe placed an ore drill on every 3x3 site in the basin, ran with production staffing autarky on, and read `seam_item` back off each one. Coal is the field thirty tiles due north behind the wall line; iron is thirty-six tiles east, which is why the smelter here runs on the sorter's byproduct instead.
three_things_this_cost_that_are_now_writ: THE HEARTH IS NOT A CONDUIT AND NOTHING ROUTES THROUGH IT. HeatFlow._route only lets a non-conductor forward heat when it is itself the source, so a burner row on the Hearth's north face reaches the four tiles it touches and nothing else. Two 220-capacity bypass mains at x112 and x143 now carry it around. Without them: generator (127,123) at output 0.00 with a full bunker under a 102-unit deficit on its own network.

THE BUILD QUEUE IS PRIORITY-ORDERED CONTENT AND IT IS A TRAP. A wall is 85, a heat pipe 80, a coal generator 60, a belt 55, an inserter 54 and a storage yard 40 — so a city that lays its grid and its wall in the first two hundred ticks has by construction put its coal yard last. Measured: the yard finished at t14841 and the belt carried its first item at t17620 while every burner starved on an empty line. `set_priority` — what a player does with a right-click — is the only reason the automation here is running before the first night.

[P05] FILLS A JOB SITE TO ITS STAFF CAPACITY, NOT TO WHAT IT REQUIRES, and hires down (build_priority desc, building id asc). Three scrap collectors placed before the sorters took twelve of the city's workers to do the work of six, and every rubble sorter behind them ran at staffing 0.00 with zero crafts for a whole run. The strip is now placed first and the collector count is two.
open: [P02] — A PRODUCER CAN BE STRANDED ON ITS OWN NETWORK, AND IT IS NOT A ROUNDING ERROR. game/sim/heat/heat_flow.gd, _route(): the multi-source BFS breaks a distance/efficiency tie on the LOWER local index, which is the lower building id, and the Hearth is id 1. A coal generator placed at (127,123) in first_night touches exactly three conduit tiles, all of which also touch the Hearth, so all three root at the Hearth for the rest of the game. _serve_tier() only reroutes over the residual graph while a constraint saturates, and the Hearth never runs out (95.7 of 134.4), so the reroute never seeds the generator. Measured across all eight checkpoints of a 24000-tick run: output 0.00, full bunker, not frozen, enabled, on a single connected network carrying a 102-unit deficit with 34 consumers browning out. Reproduce by adding `L.place(420, "coal_generator", -1, -5)` to first_night(). Worked around in the scenario by not placing a burner there, and the reason is in a comment at that line — but a player will build there, the heat lens will say the network is short, and nothing in the build will tell them why.

[P02] — AN ALERT THAT ANNOUNCES A SHORTFALL OF ZERO. heat_system.gd `_report()` fires for any deficit above 0.001 (line 926) and formats it with %.0f (line 948), so at t16109, t21627 and t22501 this run raised a severity-1 warning reading 'Network 1 short 0 heat/s — 5 buildings starved' while heat.deficit was 0.31, 0.38 and 0.08. Three of 141 alerts of that shape. This is why `heat_shortfall_is_real.implies_min` in tests/gate/expectations.json now reads 0.05 rather than 0.5 — the concession is documented in full in that band's why, and the number to restore is 0.5. It only surfaced now because the old reference run's permanent 102-unit deficit masked it in every sample.

[P03]/[P04] — THE BELT CANNOT FEED A MACHINE AND CANNOT DRAIN ONE. ProductionSystem opened both doors (offer_input at production_system.gd:311, take_output at :326) and tests/production/test_production.gd:775 exercises them. LogisticsSystem has no `accept_output` method at all, so ProductionSystem._has_accept_output is permanently false and nothing in game/ ever calls offer_input. Every machine in this game is therefore fed out of the shared city ledger by porters; a belt can carry fuel into a burner's bunker and items between chests, and that is the whole of it. That is why the automation in this scenario is a FUEL chain rather than a factory: scrap does not ride a belt into a sorter today because there is no code that would take it off. Owner is [P03] (game/sim/logistics/logistics_system.gd) and it is the single largest hole between this build and the Factorio bar.

[P05] — AN OUTPOST IS CREWED LAST AND THE DRILL FELT IT. production.ipm.coal first reads nonzero at t16780 — day three — although the drill completes on day one. It is thirty tiles out, it is heat priority 55, and the hiring order reaches it only after every kitchen, turret and collector is full to CAPACITY. A city of fifty-seven cannot crew a drill, a smelter, two sorters, a kitchen, a collector, eight turrets and a survey hall at once, which may be the correct Frostpunk answer — but nothing in the interface says 'this is why your drill is dark' and the machine reports `unstaffed` without saying who took the crew.

THE FOOD CHAIN IS HALF-CLOSED ON PURPOSE AND A FOURTH DAY WOULD NEED A SECOND SORTER. One rubble_sorter on salvaged_stores makes 0.2 grain/s and one field_kitchen eats 0.4, so across three days the founders' 1600-grain store covers the other half and ends at 1248. The band asserts produced.grain as well as produced.ration for exactly this reason — a ration count alone cannot tell a closed chain from a full larder. If first_night is ever extended past day four somebody has to add the second sorter and the workers to run it.

PERF NOT MEASURED BY ME. tools/check.sh reported stress_1000 at 69 ticks/s against a floor of 100 and smoke at 268 against 300, with its own warning that two other Godot processes were running. I changed neither scenario. first_night measured 373 ticks/s and its expects floor is set to 250 with the reason written in gen_scenarios.py. The integrator has to re-read all three alone.

tests/feel/feel_gallery.tscn FAILS 3 of 3 READS ('reduce motion: the same 33 anchors stay lit ... (32)'), and tests/feel/feel_perf.tscn flaps 2 of 3. Neither reads tests/scenarios/ — feel_gallery builds its world from game/boot.gd opening_commands() — so neither can be caused by this part. [P15]'s own comment above that assertion already describes it as a rebuild race it thought it had settled.

[P13]/[P14]/[P17] — THE FRAME THIS RUN NOW OFFERS. There are eleven shots instead of seven and the last four are day two and day three: second_day_factory (12800), second_dusk (15200), second_night (17600), third_day_city (21600). The city they photograph is a different shape from the old one — a row of six lit burners along the Hearth's faces with a belt threading under two heat mains, a salvage strip north of it, and two districts hanging off a rung to the south. If anything in view/ or ui/ was framed against the old first_night, it is worth re-shooting.
